ogTitle: Damba: chiefs on horseback in Dagbon
subtitle: Chiefs on horseback, in the month of the Prophet
answer: Damba is the biggest festival of Dagbon in the Northern Region, also kept by Mamprugu, Gonja and Wa. It falls in the month of Damba, the third month of the lunar year (Rabi al-Awwal), which marks the birth and naming of the Prophet Muhammad, though today it mostly celebrates chieftaincy: chiefs in smocks ride decorated horses to drumming and dancing before the Ya-Naa at Yendi.

sections.title: When is Damba?
sections.html: Damba follows the lunar calendar: it falls in the Dagomba month of Damba, which matches Rabi al-Awwal, the third month of the Islamic year, so it comes about eleven days earlier each year.[[2,3]] In 2019 the Yendi celebration was in mid-November; in 2026 the month began in mid-August.[[1]]

days.label: Day 10

days.html: The festival opens with the Somo Damba.[[1]]

days.label: Day 17
days.title: Naa Damba
days.html: The chiefs’ Damba, with sub-chiefs riding decorated horses with their retinues, drumming and dancing.[[1]]

days.label: Day 18
days.title: Bielkulsi
days.html: The climax, at the Gbewaa Palace durbar grounds in Yendi, presided over by the Ya-Naa, the overlord of Dagbon.[[1]]

sections.title: What Damba means
sections.html:
Damba began as a marking of the Prophet Muhammad’s birth and naming, and has grown into a celebration of chieftaincy and Dagbon’s history.[[2,3]] Dagbon sources credit its beginnings to the reign of Naa Zanjina, though it may be older.[[3]]

A chieftaincy dispute kept Damba from being held in Yendi for seventeen years; it returned in November 2019 after a new Ya-Naa was enskinned.[[1]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Tamale is the easiest base; Yendi is about two hours east, with the main durbar at the Gbewaa Palace.
Horses: riders and their retinues move fast through the crowd. Keep to the edges.
Dress: smocks (batakari) are everywhere. Modest dress is respectful in Yendi and Tamale.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

faq.a: In the month of Damba, the third month of the lunar year (Rabi al-Awwal). It moves about eleven days earlier each year; in 2026 it fell in late August and early September.
It began as a marking of the Prophet Muhammad’s birth and naming and now mainly celebrates chieftaincy in Dagbon and its neighbours.

faq.q: Where is the main Damba festival?
faq.a: At the Gbewaa Palace in Yendi, seat of the Ya-Naa, with celebrations in Tamale and across the north.
